cards.title: Two Identical Systems. One Number Decides Their Fate.
cards.dek: λ tells you how fast nearly-identical starting conditions drift apart — and whether prediction is even possible.
cards.quote: λ > 0: trajectories diverge exponentially. Chaos. λ = 0: periodic motion. λ < 0: stable, predictable.
bullets: λ quantifies the exponential separation rate of nearby trajectories
λ < 0 means convergence — the system settles toward a fixed state
λ = 0 means periodicity — trajectories hold their separation
λ > 0 means chaos — deterministic but unpredictable in the long term

cards.title: The Butterfly Doesn't Cause the Tornado
cards.dek: A positive Lyapunov exponent means the growth of uncertainty is exponential — not that tiny causes create huge effects arbitrarily.
cards.quote: For weather systems, λ ≈ 0.9 per day. A perturbation doubles in size roughly every 18 hours.
bullets: Exponential divergence, not unbounded growth — that's the real meaning of chaos
Weather is unpredictable beyond 10-14 days not because models are bad, but because uncertainty compounds exponentially
The butterfly shifts initial conditions; exponential divergence does the rest
This is why long-range weather prediction is physically impossible, not just practically difficult

cards.title: λ Is Being Used to Predict Seizures, Market Crashes, and Grid Failures
cards.dek: The Lyapunov exponent isn't just theoretical — it's a real diagnostic tool applied across biology, finance, and engineering.
cards.quote: EEG readings show characteristic Lyapunov exponent shifts 15-30 minutes before seizures.
bullets: Epilepsy: λ analysis of brain activity provides seizure early warning
Power grids: cascade failures can be detected minutes before they become inevitable
Finance: fat tails in market returns emerge from slightly positive λ — not Gaussian randomness
Neural networks: learning is most effective at λ ≈ 0, the edge of chaos
